newsitem.title: UK: Imperial Tobacco says sees bright future.
newsitem.headline: Imperial Tobacco says sees bright future.

text.p: Gareth Davies, chief executive of Imperial Tobacco Group Plc, de-merged from Hanson Plc in October, said on Thursday he believed the company's future is bright. "We believe that Imperial Tobacco's low cost production base will enable the group to pursue its strategy of expanding international sales into profitable markets," he said.

Despite successive increases in tax duty imposed on cigarettes in Britain, including an increase of 15 to 20 pence on a price of packet of 20 cigarettes in Chancellor Kenneth Clarke's November budget statement, Davies said Imperial has managed to maintain its sales by increasing its market share.

The remarks were attached to Imperial's results for the year ended September 28, which showed a five percent increase in its profits before tax and interest to 366 million pounds ($594.1 million). The company said it was confident of seeing off lawsuits bought against it by plaintiffs who allege their health has been damanged by smoking its products.

Imperial's share of the British cigarette market rose to 38.2 percent up from 37.1 percent. The trend in Britain away from higher priced brands continued, which benefitted sales of Lambert & Butler cigarettes, giving it an 11 percent share of the total market. Profits from overseas business rose 55 percent to 70 million, representing 19 percent of total group trading profit. In an interview shortly after the company's results, Edwards said Imperial aims to earn 25 percent of its profits from outside Britain by the year 2000. Imperial announced its plan to payout one third of its total annual dividend at the half year stage in August 1997 and the rest in February 1998. ($1=.6161 Pound)
